lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: proving angle properties of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle
lessonRef.title: Concept model B: proving angle properties of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Compare these two examples. Find the step where they stop being the same.

items.prompt: An inscribed angle intercepts a 100° arc. Find it.

steps: Inscribed angle is half the arc.

items.prompt: Radius 3, external point 5 from centre. Tangent length?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 2. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 45°, in terms of π.
A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 103°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 38°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 5. From an external point 13 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 8, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
12, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
12, because the tangent bisects the radius
18, because the tangent extends beyond the circle

items.prompt: A circle has radius 8. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 45°, in terms of π.
A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 125°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 76°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 3. From an external point 5 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 4, because the tangent bisects the radius
4, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
8, because the tangent extends beyond the circle
2, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency

items.prompt: A circle has radius 7. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 120°, in terms of π.
